about.title: About
about.p1Html: I'm Aron Jake Radam (also known online as ), a Lead Full-Stack Software Engineer and College Instructor working across production software and game development. I started out in game playtesting and QA at GridLock-Games Studio, testing builds, reporting bugs, and working with developers and designers ahead of releases.
about.haruOriginHtml: Haru means "spring" in Japanese (and started as a Genshin Impact in-game name given to me by someone close at the time), Chan is a subtle nod to Discord users who used to mistake me for a woman, and Z64 is for Zelda 64—The Legend of Zelda: Majora's Mask was the first Zelda game I ever played, followed by The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, on a friend's N64. Over time it became my consistent handle across GitHub and socials—a small personal brand of my own.
about.p2Html: Right now, I'm the sole full-stack engineer at PicStar Software OPC—a startup company based in Las Piñas, Philippines, building PicStar with Flutter and Supabase—from the mobile UI and PostgreSQL backend to real-time Top and Board feeds, Shineouts, rankings, and city-based filtering.
about.p3Html: Alongside industry work, I teach sophomore through senior students at the University of Caloocan City, covering game design theory, prototyping, OOP, math in games, AI, networking, and production pipelines while guiding their projects from initial mechanics to full production.
about.p4Html: Outside of my main stack, I study game design theory and build personal projects with C# (.NET), Java (Spring Boot), and Docker. I also use AI coding tools in my daily workflow to prototype and debug faster, and I'm open to freelance work or new roles.

0.b0: Teach game design theory, prototyping, and production pipelines to sophomore through senior students, guiding projects from initial mechanics to full production.
0.b1: Lead lectures and lab sessions on game programming, networking, and production, helping students turn game ideas into working builds.
0.b2: Cover core scripting and engine fundamentals including OOP, math in games, physics, collision detection, AI, networking, and code optimization.
0.b3: Manage lab sessions, guide student project progress and help with questions, and keep coursework grounded in current industry practices.

1.b0: Owned the technical direction and day-to-day engineering of a social media mobile application as the sole engineer, from architecture through deployment.
1.b1: Built the cross-platform mobile app in Flutter with a modular codebase and consistent UI/UX.
1.b2: Designed and maintained the Supabase PostgreSQL backend, tuning queries, data egress, and real-time feeds.
1.b3: Implemented core PicStar features including the Top and Board feeds, Shineouts for promoting posts and shots from Board to Top, Top rankings, and city-based content filtering.

2.b0: Worked with developers and designers to test builds and catch issues before release.
2.b1: Logged, reproduced, and tracked bugs in Trello to keep fixes moving smoothly.
2.b2: Supported the full release cycle through regression testing and build verification.

3.b0: Playtested different game builds to find bugs, glitches, and exploits.
3.b1: Gave written and verbal feedback on gameplay mechanics, balance, and overall feel.
3.b2: Worked with developers to report issues clearly and verify fixes.

0.degree: BS in Entertainment and Multimedia Computing
0.b0: Developed Trash Frenzy for our capstone project, an educational game for Grade 5 students and above that raises water pollution awareness in the Philippines and teaches proper waste disposal through storytelling and gameplay.
0.b1: Served as Project Manager, Game Designer, Game Programmer, and Game QA in a four-member team—coordinating project milestones, designing gameplay mechanics and narrative flow, implementing core systems, and testing builds for quality assurance.
0.b2: Completed coursework in Introduction to Game Design and Development, Advanced Game Design, Game Programming 1–3, Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Games, Applied Mathematics for Games, Game Networking, and Game Production.
